solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: I fantasise about everything under the sun (10)

definitions.text: I fantasise about everything under the sun
definitions.note: The clue speaks as the answer: 'I' am the daydreamer.

blocks.note: reads as someone whose fantasies cover every subject there is
the setter means literally beneath the sun, in daylight: this dreamer does it by day

annotation.surface: A confession from someone whose imagination roams over absolutely everything.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Everything under the sun' reads as 'all topics'; cryptically, 'under the sun' means in daylight, so this fantasist dreams by day.
annotation.definitionFit: A daydreamer fantasises while awake, in the daytime.

entries.clue: Troubles making love lead to icy insults (4)

indicators.note: the troubles word is made into something else by the swap
the lead of 'icy' is its first letter

blocks.note: to dog = to trouble or plague
love = O, the zero score in tennis; this is the letter swapped out
the lead (first letter) of icy, swapped in for the O

annotation.surface: Romance soured, with frosty put-downs now the only thing a couple exchanges.
annotation.walkthrough: Take DOGS and turn its love, O, into the I that leads 'icy': DOGS becomes DIGS.
annotation.definitionFit: Digs are pointed remarks, small verbal insults.

entries.clue: Chicken on top of stove turns golden (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: chicken = yellow, cowardly
first letter of stove, placed below in this down answer

annotation.surface: A cooking note: the chicken on the hob is browning nicely.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chicken' is the cowardly adjective, not the bird on the stove.
annotation.definitionFit: To yellow is to take on a golden colour, as old paper or leaves do.

entries.clue: I will show you the first of these things (5,8)

definitions.text: I will show you the first of these things

blocks.note: reads as a speaker offering a demonstration
the setter means the clue's opening letter itself: read as a number, that single stroke is 1, the first of a set of symbols

annotation.surface: Someone offering to demonstrate the first item in a series.
annotation.walkthrough: 'I' looks like the speaker, but it is the letter I, which is 1, the first Roman numeral.
annotation.definitionFit: The numerals I, II, III... are written with letters, and I is the first of them.

entries.clue: During fall, Altman shot around one uni, then another (8)

definitions.note: An adjective; 'during fall' works as in 'autumnal (during-fall) weather'.

indicators.note: a shot item is ruined and ready to be rearranged
the rearranged ALTMAN goes around the two Us

blocks.note: anagram fodder
U = university
a second U

annotation.surface: Film-making news: Robert Altman shooting in autumn around a couple of universities.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shot' fits the film director Altman so neatly that it hides its job; 'fall' is the American word for autumn.
annotation.definitionFit: Autumnal means of or during autumn, which Americans call the fall.

entries.clue: After knight leaves, tidy up and put away food (5)

definitions.note: EATEN is the participle: food 'put away' has been eaten.

indicators.note: the knight leaves, so N is removed

blocks.note: to neaten is to tidy up
N = knight in chess notation; removed from NEATEN

annotation.surface: Once the knight has gone, the servants clear up and put the leftovers away.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put away' reads as storing food in the larder; here it means eating it.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: putting food away is informal for eating it, and the participle describes the food once consumed.

entries.clue: Toothy type conservative Gordon Bennett backed (4)

indicators.note: backed = turned back to front

blocks.note: C = Conservative
both are exclamations of surprise; turned back it gives ROC

annotation.surface: A toothy Tory politician getting the support of someone called Gordon Bennett.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gordon Bennett!' is a British exclamation of astonishment, like 'Cor!'; 'backed' reads as supported, not reversed.
annotation.definitionFit: A croc (crocodile) is a creature famous for its teeth.

entries.clue: Buy the farm if interior of study gets fitted out (7)

indicators.note: DIE goes into the interior of READ
READ gets DIE put inside it

blocks.note: to read a subject is to study it; opened up as REA...D
'buy the farm' is American slang for dying

annotation.surface: A farmhouse purchase that goes ahead if the study is kitted out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Buy the farm' looks like a property deal; it is slang for dying.
annotation.definitionFit: Something readied has been prepared, fitted out for use.

entries.clue: Can we sleep after seismic event and landslide? (5,5)

indicators.note: after an earthquake everything is shaken up, so the letters are too

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

annotation.surface: Anxious residents wondering whether they can rest after an earthquake and a landslip.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Landslide' sits beside 'seismic event' as a natural disaster; it is the election kind.
annotation.definitionFit: A landslide victory wins everything, a clean sweep.

entries.clue: Maine journal rebuffed one with feet of clay (5)

indicators.note: re-buffed, pushed back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: ME = Maine, US state abbreviation
a log is a journal

annotation.surface: A Maine newspaper turning away a flawed figure.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Feet of clay' suggests a hidden flaw; the golem of Jewish legend is literally made of clay.
annotation.definitionFit: A golem is a figure moulded from clay and brought to life.

entries.clue: Tickle flipping relations into the small hours? (9)

indicators.note: flipping turns IT over to TI

blocks.note: IT = sex, as 'relations' does too
til late = until late at night

annotation.surface: Some cheeky relations tickle each other until the early morning.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Relations' looks like family but means sexual relations, IT; 'flipping' also works as a mild curse.
annotation.definitionFit: To titillate is to tickle, literally or by arousing interest.

entries.clue: Lag delights in messing around authorities (7,6)

indicators.note: the letters are messed about

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

annotation.surface: An old prisoner happily winds up the prison bosses.
annotation.walkthrough: A lag is a convict, so the authorities look like the prison warders, but they are the fodder's own anagram.
annotation.definitionFit: Leading lights are prominent figures, authorities in their field.

entries.clue: Garnish on a rotten main wants spicing up (13)

indicators.note: the letters need livening up, mixing

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

annotation.surface: A restaurant critic: the garnish on a poor main course can't hide that it needs more flavour.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rotten' looks like the anagram indicator but is part of the fodder; the indicator is 'wants spicing up'.
annotation.definitionFit: Garnish is decoration, ornamentation, added to food or anything else.

entries.clue: In league A, field a fit Batty (10)

indicators.note: batty = crazy, so the letters go mad

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

annotation.surface: A cricket instruction: in the top division, put out a fit side to bat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'League', 'field' and 'Batty' all point at cricket or football, and 'Batty' looks like a player's name.
annotation.definitionFit: Affiliated means officially connected, in league with.

entries.clue: Duke you left by a river of reeds, perhaps (8)

blocks.note: dukes = fists, old slang
text-speak you
L = left
as printed
R = river

annotation.surface: A duke leaves someone beside a reed-lined river.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Duke' looks like a nobleman; 'put up your dukes' means raise your fists.
annotation.definitionFit: Fistular means hollow and tube-shaped, as reeds are.

entries.clue: Light breeze over the eastern side of Barrow (6)

indicators.note: in an across entry the eastern (right-hand) side is the last letter

blocks.note: a breeze is a light wind
O = over, cricket scoring
last letter of Barrow

annotation.surface: A gentle breeze drifting across the east of Barrow, a Cumbrian town.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Light breeze' reads as one phrase; 'Light' is the definition and only 'breeze' is wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: An architectural sense: a light is any opening or pane that lets daylight into a building.

entries.clue: Dynasty over at last, first parts of Cops on next (6,2)

indicators.note: take the first letters of the next two words

blocks.note: first letters of Cops and on
the Ming dynasty of China
over at last, as in 'time's up'

annotation.surface: A TV schedule: the drama series Dynasty is finally over and the cop show comes next.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a TV listing, with Dynasty and Cops as shows; the definition 'next' is the continuity announcer's phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: Coming up means next, as in a broadcaster's 'coming up after the break'.

entries.clue: One with busy people nursing ten beastly types (6)

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so BEES hold X

blocks.note: I = one, Roman numeral
busy as a bee; opened up as BE...ES
X = ten, Roman numeral

annotation.surface: A carer among busy staff looking after ten unruly animals.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Busy people' are bees, not humans.
annotation.definitionFit: Ibexes are wild mountain goats, types of beast.

entries.clue: Sovereign contrary agent hid in foreign capital (7)

indicators.note: contrary = the other way round, so the result is turned back
to hide in something is to be concealed within it, so REP goes inside ROME

blocks.note: the Italian capital, foreign to a British solver; opened up as RO...ME
a rep = a representative, an agent

annotation.surface: A spy story: a king's double agent lying low in a foreign city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sovereign' could be the gold coin; here it is the ruler, and 'contrary agent' teases the double agent.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the ruler of an empire is its supreme monarch, the highest kind of sovereign.

entries.clue: Inferior E, perhaps (3-5)

blocks.note: an adjective: poor in quality, second-rate
an E is a mark near the bottom of an exam scale, given by example

annotation.walkthrough: E is a low grade in a school or exam marking scale, so 'E, perhaps' describes the answer by example.
annotation.definitionFit: Low-grade means inferior in quality; an E is literally a low grade.

entries.clue: When you want a lot of unopened porridge (7)

indicators.note: MANY without its opening letter

blocks.note: a lot of = MANY, which unopened drops its M
porridge is British slang for a prison sentence, time

annotation.surface: A breakfast offer: have as much porridge as you like, whenever.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Porridge' sits there as breakfast; in British slang doing porridge means serving time in prison.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the informal adverb for at whatever moment suits the person asking.

entries.clue: Wild claim about power, skill and relentlessness (13)

indicators.note: wild = uncontrolled, so CLAIM's letters are scrambled
the rearranged CLAIM goes about P

blocks.note: CLAIM rearranged, opened up as IM...LAC
P = power
skill = ability

annotation.surface: Someone boasting of their strength, talent and never giving up.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a boastful list of virtues; the last one, 'relentlessness', is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Implacability is the quality of being impossible to appease, relentless.

entries.clue: Excellent work secures Magnus’s first mate in Spain (5)

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so A1 holds the M inside it
Magnus's first means the first letter of that name

blocks.note: A1 = excellent, the 1 written as I; opened up as A...I
first letter of Magnus
to go = to work, function

annotation.surface: A chess report: Magnus Carlsen's brilliant play delivers mate in a Spanish tournament.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mate' looks like checkmate from the world champion Magnus Carlsen; it is the friend sense, in Spanish.
annotation.definitionFit: A foreign-language definition: the Spanish word for friend, and mate is British for friend.

entries.clue: Does dope in America finally graduate classes? (4)

indicators.note: the final letters of the next two words

blocks.note: US = America
last letters of graduate and classes

annotation.surface: A question about drug-taking at American college graduation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Does' looks like a verb of doing; with 'dope' it means takes drugs, which is what 'uses' means.
annotation.definitionFit: To use is slang for taking drugs, so 'does dope' is 'uses'.

entries.clue: Object, having to take ill-considered punishment? (9)

indicators.note: THING takes RASH inside it

blocks.note: an object is a thing; opened up as TH...ING
rash = ill-considered, hasty

annotation.surface: Someone protesting at having to accept a hasty, badly judged penalty.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a verb, to protest; it is the noun, a thing.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a severe beating given as a penalty.

entries.clue: Those first in lines of songs on the radio (5)

indicators.note: heard over the airwaves, so what counts is the sound

blocks.note: airs = songs, tunes

annotation.surface: Opening lines of songs being played on the radio.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lines' reads as lyrics; it means lines of succession, which heirs are first in.
annotation.definitionFit: Heirs stand first in line to inherit a title or estate.

entries.clue: One heading to bed on board craft on delta (4)

definitions.text: One heading to bed on board

blocks.note: Delta = D in the NATO alphabet
a craft is an art or skill

annotation.surface: A passenger going to their bunk aboard a vessel on a river delta.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'bed' is a scoring segment of a dartboard, such as the treble bed, and a dart is thrown at it; 'craft' looks like a boat.
annotation.definitionFit: A dart flies to a bed (double or treble ring) on the dartboard.

entries.clue: Tenor kidnapped by Brahms and Liszt? Rotters! (10)

indicators.note: T is carried off inside COMPOSERS

blocks.note: both are composers; opened up as COMPOS...ERS
T = tenor

annotation.surface: An outraged cry at two great composers abducting a tenor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rotters' reads as an insult; composters are things that make waste rot. 'Brahms and Liszt' is also rhyming slang for drunk, a second red herring.
annotation.definitionFit: Composters rot garden waste down, so they are literally rotters.
